```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
# R code here is ASCII only (HTML entities for special characters), so the page renders the same in any locale
A <- "docs/assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum"
tq <- fread(file.path(A, "tissue_qtls.tsv")); st <- fread(file.path(A, "isoform_steps.tsv")); it <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_steps.tsv"))
dc <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_copies.tsv"))
pa <- fread(file.path(A, "params.tsv")); g <- fread(file.path(A, "gene_pips.tsv")); cv <- fread(file.path(A, "convergence.tsv"))
RUNS <- c(es="eQTL + sQTL", esi="eQTL + sQTL + irQTL", i="irQTL only", est="eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 1)", t="isoQTL only (top 1)",
          esh="eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 3)", h="isoQTL only (top 3)", esf="eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 5)", f="isoQTL only (top 5)")
TYPES <- list(es=c("eQTL", "sQTL"), esi=c("eQTL", "sQTL", "irQTL"), i="irQTL", est=c("eQTL", "sQTL", "isoQTL"), t="isoQTL",
              esh=c("eQTL", "sQTL", "isoQTL"), h="isoQTL", esf=c("eQTL", "sQTL", "isoQTL"), f="isoQTL")
# only the runs this page shows
dc <- dc[run %in% names(RUNS)]; pa <- pa[run %in% names(RUNS)]; g <- g[run %in% names(RUNS)]; cv <- cv[run %in% names(RUNS)]
TOP1 <- c("es", "esi", "i", "est", "t")
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
fp <- function(x) vapply(x, function(z) if (is.na(z)) "NA" else format(signif(z, 2)), "")
cell <- function(x) fifelse(is.na(x), "&ndash;", sprintf("%.2f", x))
iso <- pa[run == "esi" & type == "irQTL"]; isq <- pa[run == "t" & type == "isoQTL"]
cb <- tq[tissue == "Brain_Cerebellum"]
g8 <- function(r) g[run == r & combined_pip >= 0.8, gene_name]
# one run's genes: a PIP column per QTL type only when the run has more than one type; isoQTL runs add the duplicate count
gene_table <- function(r, d) {
  d <- d[order(-combined_pip)]; x <- d[, .(gene_name, combined_pip=sprintf("%.2f", combined_pip))]
  if (length(TYPES[[r]]) > 1) for (k in TYPES[[r]]) x[[paste0(k, "_pip")]] <- cell(d[[paste0(k, "_pip")]])
  x <- cbind(x, d[, .(Traits=n_traits, `Top trait`=top_trait, `Top trait type`=top_type, `susie_pip (top trait)`=sprintf("%.2f", top_trait_pip), z=sprintf("%.1f", z))])
  if ("isoQTL" %in% TYPES[[r]]) x[, `isoQTL copies` := fifelse(is.na(d$top_isoqtl_copies), "&ndash;", as.character(d$top_isoqtl_copies))]
  paste(knitr::kable(x, escape=FALSE, align=ifelse(names(x) %in% c("gene_name", "Top trait", "Top trait type"), "l", "r")), collapse="\n")
}
```

# How we selected the tissue

We chose the brain tissue with the most isoform-ratio QTLs (irQTLs: QTLs for an
isoform's share of its gene's expression), since SCZ is a brain
trait. The counts are Pantry's conditionally independent cis-QTLs per GTEx v8
tissue (`gtex.separate_kdp.qtls.tsv.gz`, downloaded 2026-10-29).

```{r tissues}
d <- tq[brain == TRUE | rank <= 3][order(rank)]
knitr::kable(d[, .(Rank=rank, Tissue=gsub("_", " ", tissue), `Pantry code`=code, `irQTLs`=fmt(isoform_qtls),
  Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), Genes=fmt(isoform_genes), eQTLs=fmt(eqtls), `Splicing QTLs`=fmt(sqtls))], align="rllrrrrr")
```

- **Rank:** among all `r nrow(tq)` tissues, by the number of irQTLs. The
  table shows the top three tissues overall and every brain tissue.
- **irQTLs:** independent cis-QTLs; **Isoforms** and **Genes** are the
  isoforms and genes they belong to. **eQTLs** and **Splicing QTLs** are Pantry's
  expression and intron-excision QTLs in the same tissue, for comparison.

Brain Cerebellum has the most among brain tissues: `r fmt(cb$isoform_qtls)`
irQTLs in `r fmt(cb$isoforms)` isoforms of `r fmt(cb$isoform_genes)` genes.
Testis has the most overall. Pantry codes the two cerebellum tissues BRNCHA and
BRNCHB. Its covariate files have 209 samples for BRNCHA and 175 for BRNCHB, the
GTEx v8 sample sizes of Brain Cerebellum and Cerebellar Hemisphere, so BRNCHA is
Brain Cerebellum.

# How the runs were set up

- **GWAS:** PGC schizophrenia, `ieu-b-5102` (N = 127,906), z-scores harmonized to
  the UK Biobank (UKB) LD reference, as for the M-cTWAS paper.
- **eQTL and sQTL weights:** the paper's GTEx v8 PredictDB expression and splicing
  models for Brain Cerebellum.
- **irQTL weights** (our definition): one trait per isoform, from Pantry's
  independent cis-QTLs in Brain Cerebellum. They come from the genes significant
  in Pantry's permutation test, q < 0.05.
  - Each isoform's QTL is its strongest independent variant (smallest nominal p)
    among single-base variants in the UKB reference that are not
    strand-ambiguous.
  - The weight is that variant's effect on the isoform ratio (tensorQTL's
    slope); with one SNP per trait, only its sign matters.
  - Genes come from Pantry's own annotation. We used top QTLs, not Munro's
    prediction models.
- **isoQTL weights** (added 2026-11-04; models from the paper, the top SNP is ours):
  one trait per isoform, from the isoTWAS prediction models of
  [Bhattacharya et al. 2023](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-023-01560-2) for GTEx v8
  Brain Cerebellum ([Zenodo 8047940](https://zenodo.org/records/8047940)).
  - The paper's trait is one isoform's expression (Salmon, GENCODE v38), predicted
    from SNPs within 1 Mb by multivariate models fitted over all of the gene's
    isoforms. Only isoforms with cross-validated R<sup>2</sup> &ge; 0.01 are released.
  - The models are dense (median 471 SNPs per isoform). We kept the SNP with
    the largest standardised weight per isoform (top 1), or the 5 SNPs with the
    largest (top 5, added 2026-11-04 at Xin's suggestion), or the 3 largest (top 3,
    added 2026-11-05): see
    [How the isoQTL SNP was chosen](#how-the-isoqtl-snp-was-chosen).
  - Genes are named from the paper's PredictDB mapping (as for eQTLs), else from
    Pantry's annotation.
- **Settings, as the paper's runs:** each QTL type is its own group, with protein-coding genes only and LD
  from the UKB reference. eQTL and sQTL weights are scaled (`scale_predictdb_weights`), and
  so are the top-3 and top-5 isoQTL weights, whose SNPs' relative weights matter. The top-1 isoform
  weights (irQTL and isoQTL) are not scaled: with one SNP per trait only the sign matters.
  No thinning, one prior variance shared by all groups (`shared_all`), up to 5 signals per
  region (L = 5).
- **Nine runs:** eQTL + sQTL (the paper's QTL types), eQTL + sQTL + irQTL,
  irQTL only (added 2026-11-03, to test whether the irQTLs
  carry signal on their own), and eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL and isoQTL only, each
  with the top 1, top 3 and top 5 SNPs per isoform (added 2026-11-04 and
  2026-11-05). All use the same settings.
- **Post-processing** (region merging and the LD-mismatch check, added 2026-11-07)
  for the three eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL runs (top 1, 3, 5): see
  [Post-processing](#post-processing). **Not done yet:** merging
  [duplicate isoQTL traits](#duplicate-isoqtl-traits).

```{r steps}
knitr::kable(st[, .(Step=step, QTLs=fmt(qtls), Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), Genes=fmt(genes))], align="lrrr")
```

The irQTL weights at each step. The last row is the weights. cTWAS then
keeps the isoforms of protein-coding genes whose QTL is in the GWAS:
`r fmt(iso$group_size)` traits.

```{r isoqtl_steps}
knitr::kable(it[, .(Step=step, `Isoform-SNP pairs`=fmt(rows), Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), Genes=fmt(genes))], align="lrrr")
```

```{r isoqtl_top5_steps}
s5 <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top5_steps.tsv")); s5 <- s5[nrow(s5)]; isf <- pa[run == "f" & type == "isoQTL"]
```

The isoQTL weights at each step (top 1); the first row counts every isoform-SNP pair in
the released models. cTWAS keeps the protein-coding isoforms whose SNP is in the
GWAS: `r fmt(isq$group_size)` traits. The top-5 weights pass the same steps and
keep `r fmt(s5$rows)` isoform-SNP pairs for the same `r fmt(s5$isoforms)`
protein-coding isoforms. cTWAS keeps `r fmt(isf$group_size)` of them: cTWAS drops a
weight's SNPs that are not in the GWAS, and the trait survives while one of its 5
SNPs remains. The top-3 weights are built the same way; cTWAS keeps
`r fmt(pa[run == "h" & type == "isoQTL", group_size])` of them.

## How the isoQTL SNP was chosen

```{r topsnp_setup}
ts <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top_share.tsv")); ex <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top_snp_example.tsv"))
ta <- ts[usable_snps == "all"]; big <- ts[usable_snps == "more than 500"]; small <- ts[usable_snps == "1-20"]
pc <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
```

Each released isoTWAS file is one gene: one row per isoform and SNP, with the
SNP's model weight (`Weight`) and the isoform model's cross-validated R<sup>2</sup>.
We kept one SNP per isoform (our choice; `4.build_isoqtl_isotwas.R`):

1. Keep isoforms with R<sup>2</sup> &ge; 0.01 and SNPs with a non-zero weight
   (all released models pass).
2. Keep the usable SNPs: single-base, autosomal, in the UKB b38 reference (same
   position, alleles in either orientation) and not strand-ambiguous (A/T, C/G).
3. Standardise each weight: |weight| &times; the SNP's genotype SD in the UKB
   reference. The isoTWAS weights are per copy of the counted allele (the models
   were trained on 0/1/2 genotypes, not standardised), so a rare SNP can have a
   large weight yet move the predicted expression little. The standardised
   weight measures how much the SNP moves the prediction across people.
4. Keep the SNP with the largest standardised weight (ties: the smaller
   position). Its weight goes into cTWAS unchanged; with one SNP per trait only
   its sign matters.

This is the model's most influential SNP, not a QTL lead variant: the released
files have no association statistics.

**Example:** `r ex$gene_name[1]`'s isoform `r sub(".*__", "", ex$molecular_id[1])`, the
trait behind `r ex$gene_name[1]` in the joint run. It has `r fmt(ex$usable_snps[1])` usable
SNPs; these are the 10 with the largest standardised weight.

```{r topsnp_example}
knitr::kable(ex[, .(Rank=rank_std, `Rank by |weight|`=rank_raw, SNP=snp, Position=fmt(pos), `Counted allele`=counted_allele, `Other allele`=other_allele,
  Weight=sprintf("%.4f", weight), MAF=sprintf("%.3f", maf), `Genotype SD`=sprintf("%.2f", sd), `Standardised weight`=sprintf("%.4f", std_weight),
  top_share=pc(top_share), `Cumulative share`=pc(cum_share))], align="rrlrllrrrrrr")
```

- **Rank:** by standardised weight; **Rank by |weight|:** by the raw weight
  (tied weights share a rank).
- **Counted allele:** the allele the weight is per copy of (the file's `REF`
  column, which the isoTWAS training code counts). **MAF** and **Genotype SD**
  come from the UKB reference.
- **top_share** (ours): the SNP's standardised weight over the sum for all the
  isoform's usable SNPs; **Cumulative share** adds them down the table.

The chosen SNP, `r ex$snp[1]`, is only third by raw weight: `r ex[rank_raw == 1, snp]` has
the largest weight but MAF `r sprintf("%.3f", ex[rank_raw == 1, maf])`. It carries
`r pc(ex$top_share[1])` of the model, about as much as the next SNP
(`r pc(ex$top_share[2])`). Half of the model's weight needs `r ex$snps_for_half[1]` SNPs,
and `r fmt(ex$snps_below_0.1pct[1])` of the `r fmt(ex$usable_snps[1])` SNPs carry less
than 0.1% each.

```{r topsnp_share}
k5 <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top5_kept.tsv")); stopifnot(identical(k5$usable_snps, ts$usable_snps), identical(k5$isoforms, ts$isoforms))
ts <- cbind(ts, k5[, .(median_kept_share, q25_kept_share, q75_kept_share, fewer_than_5_snps)])
ka <- ts[usable_snps == "all"]; big <- ts[usable_snps == "more than 500"]
knitr::kable(ts[, .(`Usable SNPs per model`=usable_snps, Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), `Median usable SNPs`=fmt(median_usable_snps),
  `top_share, median`=pc(median_top_share), `top_share, 25%-75%`=sprintf("%s-%s", pc(q25_top_share), pc(q75_top_share)),
  `kept_share (top 5), median`=pc(median_kept_share), `kept_share (top 5), 25%-75%`=sprintf("%s-%s", pc(q25_kept_share), pc(q75_kept_share)))],
  align="lrrrrrr")
```

- **kept_share (top 5)** (ours): the summed standardised weight of the 5 SNPs
  kept per isoform, over the sum for all its usable SNPs.

Over all `r fmt(ta$isoforms)` isoforms the models fall into two kinds: small
models (`r fmt(small$isoforms)` isoforms with at most 20 usable SNPs), where the
chosen SNP carries a median `r pc(small$median_top_share)` of the weight, and
large models (`r fmt(big$isoforms)` isoforms with more than 500 usable SNPs, median
`r fmt(big$median_usable_snps)`), where it carries `r pc(big$median_top_share)`. For the second kind one SNP is a
poor summary of the model.

**Top 5** (added 2026-11-04, Xin's suggestion): the same steps, keeping the 5 SNPs
with the largest standardised weight per isoform, each with its model weight
(`4.build_isoqtl_isotwas.R` with K = 5). The `r fmt(ka$fewer_than_5_snps)` isoforms
with fewer than 5 usable SNPs keep all of them. The 5 SNPs carry a median
`r pc(ka$median_kept_share)` of the weight, against `r pc(ka$median_top_share)`
for the top SNP, but only `r pc(big$median_kept_share)` in the large models.

## What the tables and figures show

**Parameters**, the output of `summarize_param()`:

- **group_size:** molecular traits that reach cTWAS after matching to the GWAS and the LD reference.
- **group_prior:** the estimated prior probability that a trait (or a SNP) is causal.
- **group_prior_var:** the prior variance of a causal effect, shared by all groups (`shared_all`).
- **log_enrichment:** the log of a group's prior over the SNP prior, with its
  standard error; **enrichment_pval** is its p-value.
- **group_pve:** the proportion of SCZ variance explained by the group;
  **total_pve** sums all groups and SNPs.
- **prop_heritability:** a group's `group_pve` over `total_pve`, the slices of the
  pie charts.

**Convergence**, from `make_convergence_plots()`: the estimates at each iteration
of the parameter estimation (proportion causal &pi; is `group_prior`, effect size
&sigma;<sup>2</sup> is `group_prior_var`, enrichment is
&pi;<sub>G</sub>/&pi;<sub>S</sub>, and PVE).

**Gene-level PIPs:** `combined_pip` combines all of a gene's molecular traits and
QTL types with `combine_gene_pips()` (`by = "type"`, `method = "combine_cs"`,
`filter_cs = FALSE`). **eQTL_pip**, **sQTL_pip**, **irQTL_pip** and **isoQTL_pip** are the gene's
PIP from each QTL type; "&ndash;" means the gene has no trait of that type in a
fine-mapped region. The mapping table assigns each trait to its gene: the paper's
PredictDB mapping for eQTL genes and sQTL introns, Pantry's annotation for
irQTL isoforms, and the PredictDB mapping (else Pantry's) for isoQTL isoforms.

# Results

## Parameters

```{r params}
w <- merge(pa[type != "SNP"], pa[type == "SNP", .(run, snp_prior=group_prior)], by="run")[order(match(run, names(RUNS)), match(type, c("eQTL", "sQTL", "irQTL", "isoQTL")))]
knitr::kable(w[, .(Run=RUNS[run], group, group_size=fmt(group_size), group_prior=sprintf("%.5f", group_prior), `group_prior (SNP)`=sprintf("%.5f", snp_prior),
  group_prior_var=sprintf("%.1f", group_prior_var), `log_enrichment (log_enrichment_se)`=sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", log_enrichment, log_enrichment_se),
  enrichment_pval=fp(enrichment_pval), group_pve=sprintf("%.4f", group_pve), total_pve=sprintf("%.3f", total_pve),
  prop_heritability=sprintf("%.5f", prop_heritability))], align="llrrrrrrrrr")
```

```{r isoqtl_note}
ij <- pa[run == "est" & type == "isoQTL"]; e0 <- pa[run == "es" & type != "SNP"]; e1 <- pa[run == "est" & type != "SNP"]
pt <- function(r, ty) pa[run == r & type == ty, group_pve / group_size]
```

**isoQTLs** (2026-11-04): unlike the irQTLs, the isoQTLs stay enriched when
eQTLs and sQTLs are in the same run.

- `log_enrichment` is `r sprintf("%.2f", isq$log_enrichment)` alone and
  `r sprintf("%.2f", ij$log_enrichment)` with eQTLs and sQTLs (`enrichment_pval`
  `r fp(ij$enrichment_pval)`); the irQTLs fall from
  `r sprintf("%.2f", pa[run == "i" & type == "irQTL", log_enrichment])` alone to
  `r sprintf("%.2f", iso$log_enrichment)`.
- In the joint run the isoQTLs take `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * ij$prop_heritability)`
  of `total_pve`, and all molecular traits together
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * sum(e1$prop_heritability))`, against
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * sum(e0$prop_heritability))` with eQTLs and sQTLs only.
- Per trait the isoQTL signal is small: `group_pve` / `group_size` (ours) is
  `r sprintf("%.1e", pt("est", "isoQTL"))`, against `r sprintf("%.1e", pt("est", "eQTL"))`
  for eQTLs in the same run. The share is large because the group is large
  (`r fmt(isq$group_size)` traits).
- These are the top-1 runs. With the top 3 / top 5 SNPs per isoform, the isoQTL
  `log_enrichment` is `r sprintf("%.2f", pa[run == "h" & type == "isoQTL", log_enrichment])` /
  `r sprintf("%.2f", pa[run == "f" & type == "isoQTL", log_enrichment])` alone and
  `r sprintf("%.2f", pa[run == "esh" & type == "isoQTL", log_enrichment])` /
  `r sprintf("%.2f", pa[run == "esf" & type == "isoQTL", log_enrichment])` jointly, and the
  isoQTLs take `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pa[run == "esh" & type == "isoQTL", prop_heritability])` /
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pa[run == "esf" & type == "isoQTL", prop_heritability])` of
  `total_pve` in the joint run. Much of this gain may be an artefact: see
  [Top 3 and top 5 SNPs per isoform: checks](#top-3-and-top-5-snps-per-isoform-checks).

## Gene-level PIPs

### Genes with combined_pip of at least 0.8 in any top-1 run

```{r overview}
gn <- sort(unique(g[run %in% TOP1 & combined_pip >= 0.8, gene_name]))
pick <- function(r, col) vapply(gn, function(x) { v <- g[run == r & gene_name == x][[col]]; if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_real_ }, 0)
o <- data.table(gene_name=gn, a=pick("es", "combined_pip"), b=pick("esi", "combined_pip"), c=pick("i", "combined_pip"), d=pick("est", "combined_pip"),
                e=pick("est", "eQTL_pip"), s=pick("est", "sQTL_pip"), t=pick("est", "isoQTL_pip"), u=pick("t", "combined_pip"),
                v=pick("esf", "combined_pip"), w=pick("f", "combined_pip"), v3=pick("esh", "combined_pip"), w3=pick("h", "combined_pip"))[order(-d)]
knitr::kable(o[, .(gene_name, `combined_pip (eQTL + sQTL)`=cell(a), `combined_pip (+ irQTL)`=cell(b), `combined_pip (irQTL only)`=cell(c),
  `combined_pip (+ isoQTL top 1)`=cell(d), `eQTL_pip (+ isoQTL top 1)`=cell(e), `sQTL_pip (+ isoQTL top 1)`=cell(s), `isoQTL_pip (+ isoQTL top 1)`=cell(t),
  `combined_pip (isoQTL top 1 only)`=cell(u), `combined_pip (+ isoQTL top 3)`=cell(v3), `combined_pip (isoQTL top 3 only)`=cell(w3),
  `combined_pip (+ isoQTL top 5)`=cell(v), `combined_pip (isoQTL top 5 only)`=cell(w))],
  escape=FALSE, align="lrrrrrrrrrrrr")
```

Columns 2&ndash;5 and 9&ndash;13 are `combined_pip` in each run; columns 6&ndash;8
split the eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 1) run's `combined_pip` by QTL type. "&ndash;"
means the gene was not in a fine-mapped region in that run, or has no trait of
that type. The table lists the genes of the top-1 runs. The top-3 and top-5 runs have
many more (`r length(g8("esh"))` and `r length(g8("esf"))` in the joint runs): see
[Top 3 and top 5 SNPs per isoform: checks](#top-3-and-top-5-snps-per-isoform-checks) and the run tabs below.

### Duplicate isoQTL traits

```{r dup_setup}
dt <- dc[run == "t"]; d5 <- function(r) dc[run == r & copy_group == "5 or more copies"]
pair <- g[run == "est" & gene_name %in% c("PPIL2", "TMEM25")][order(-combined_pip)]
ar <- g[run == "est" & gene_name == "ARHGAP9"]
```

**Caveat (ours):** with one SNP per isoform, isoforms of the same gene often get
the same top SNP. Their predicted expressions are then the same trait (up to
sign), and cTWAS keeps them as separate traits. SuSiE splits a signal evenly over
such copies and `combined_pip` adds them back, so a gene with many copies gets
the prior of many traits.

```{r dup}
knitr::kable(dc[, .(Run=RUNS[run], `Copies per gene and SNPs`=copy_group, `isoQTL traits`=fmt(traits), `Share of traits`=sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * trait_share),
  `susie_pip sum`=sprintf("%.1f", pip_sum), `Share of susie_pip`=sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * pip_share))], align="llrrrr")
```

- **Copies per gene and SNPs:** how many of the run's isoQTL traits have the same
  gene and the same SNP (top 1), or the same gene and SNPs with proportional
  weights (top 3, top 5); 1 = no duplicate.
- **susie_pip sum:** the isoQTL traits' `susie_pip`, summed over fine-mapped
  regions; **Share of susie_pip** is its share of the run's isoQTL total.
- **isoQTL copies** (gene tables below): the copies of the gene's isoQTL trait
  with the largest `susie_pip`.

The copy groups take about the same share of `susie_pip` as of traits, so the
duplicates do not drive the group estimates above. They matter for single
genes. In the eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 1) run,
`r paste(sprintf("%s (combined_pip %.2f) rests on %d copies of its top trait, each with susie_pip %.2f", pair$gene_name, pair$combined_pip, pair$top_isoqtl_copies, pair$top_isoqtl_pip), collapse=", and ")`.
Their SNPs have GWAS |z| `r paste(sprintf("%.2f", abs(pair$z)), collapse=" and ")`
(p `r paste(fp(2 * pnorm(-abs(pair$z))), collapse=" and ")`), below genome-wide significance. ARHGAP9 rests on one isoform,
`r sub(".*__", "", ar$top_trait)` (susie_pip `r sprintf("%.2f", ar$top_trait_pip)`,
z = `r sprintf("%.1f", ar$z)`).

With the top 3 or top 5 SNPs duplicates are rarer:
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * dc[run == "esh" & copy_group == "1 copy", trait_share])` and
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * dc[run == "esf" & copy_group == "1 copy", trait_share])` of the isoQTL
traits have no copy, against `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * dc[run == "est" & copy_group == "1 copy", trait_share])`
with the top SNP.

### Top 3 and top 5 SNPs per isoform: checks

```{r top5_setup}
fl <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top5_flags.tsv")); rg <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top5_region.tsv"))
ex5 <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top5_example.tsv")); ge <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top5_geometry.tsv"))
fj <- fl[run == "esf"]; f1 <- fl[run == "est"]; sn <- rg[type == "SNP (strongest)"]; rt <- rg[type != "SNP (strongest)"]
e2 <- ex5[order(-abs(weight))][1:2]; r12 <- ex5[snp == e2$snp[1]][[paste0("r_", e2$snp[2])]]
gcl <- function(k) ge[class == k]
kn <- g[run == "esf" & gene_name %in% c("CACNA1C", "CACNA1D", "MAD1L1")][order(gene_name)]
dr <- setdiff(g8("es"), g8("esf"))   # genes at >= 0.8 with eQTL + sQTL that fall below 0.8 with the top-5 isoQTLs
dr3 <- setdiff(g8("es"), g8("esh")); f3 <- fl[run == "esh"]
sh35 <- length(intersect(g8("esh"), g8("esf")))   # genes at 0.8 with both top 3 and top 5
pip_of <- function(r, x) { v <- g[run == r & gene_name == x, combined_pip]; if (length(v)) v else NA_real_ }
dr <- data.table(gene_name=dr, es=vapply(dr, function(x) g[run == "es" & gene_name == x, combined_pip], 0),
                 esf=vapply(dr, function(x) { v <- g[run == "esf" & gene_name == x, combined_pip]; if (length(v)) v else NA_real_ }, 0))
```

**Short answer (ours):** with the top 5 SNPs per isoform the isoQTLs look much
stronger, but several signs point to fine-mapping artefacts, not signal. The
top 3 SNPs (added 2026-11-05) show the same signs, so the problem comes with any
multi-SNP truncation of these models, not with 5 SNPs in particular. We have not
tested the cause. Until we have, the top-1 runs are the safer result.

- **Top 3:** in the joint run the isoQTLs take
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pa[run == "esh" & type == "isoQTL", prop_heritability])` of `total_pve`, and
  `r f3$genes_pip08` genes reach `combined_pip` &ge; 0.8, `r f3$genes_pip08_z_lt3` of them with |z| < 3.
  `r length(dr3)` of the `r length(g8("es"))` genes of the eQTL + sQTL run fall below 0.8. The gene
  list is not stable between top 3 and top 5: only `r sh35` of the `r length(g8("esh"))` genes at 0.8
  with top 3 are at 0.8 with top 5 (CACNA1C: `r sprintf("%.2f", pip_of("esh", "CACNA1C"))` with top 3,
  `r sprintf("%.2f", pip_of("esf", "CACNA1C"))` with top 5). AMT, the example below, has
  `combined_pip` `r sprintf("%.2f", pip_of("esh", "AMT"))` with top 3: its two largest weights, the
  opposite-sign pair, are also the top 2 of 3.

**Top 5** (2026-11-04):

- In the joint run the isoQTLs take
  `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pa[run == "esf" & type == "isoQTL", prop_heritability])` of `total_pve`
  (top 1: `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pa[run == "est" & type == "isoQTL", prop_heritability])`), and
  `r fj$genes_pip08` genes reach `combined_pip` &ge; 0.8 (top 1: `r f1$genes_pip08`).
- Some new genes have a strong marginal signal:
  `r paste(sprintf("%s (combined_pip %.2f, z = %.1f)", kn$gene_name, kn$combined_pip, kn$z), collapse=", ")`.
- But `r nrow(dr)` of the `r length(g8("es"))` genes of the eQTL + sQTL run fall below 0.8
  (`combined_pip` there, then with the top-5 isoQTLs):
  `r paste(sprintf("%s %.2f to %s", dr$gene_name, dr$es, cell(dr$esf)), collapse=", ")`.

```{r top5_flags}
knitr::kable(fl[match(c("es", "est", "t", "esh", "h", "esf", "f"), run), .(Run=RUNS[run], `Regions fine-mapped`=fmt(regions), `Genes, combined_pip >= 0.8`=genes_pip08,
  `of which |z| < 3`=genes_pip08_z_lt3, `Regions, traits take > 3 effects`=regions_trait_pip_gt3, `of which no SNP p < 5e-8`=regions_trait_pip_gt3_no_gws_snp)],
  align="lrrrrr")
```

All columns are ours.

- **of which |z| < 3:** genes whose top trait has a GWAS z-score below 3 in
  absolute value. A causal gene should show a marginal association.
- **Regions, traits take > 3 effects:** regions where the molecular traits'
  `susie_pip` sums to more than 3, so SuSiE puts more than 3 of its 5 effects on
  molecular traits. **of which no SNP p < 5e-8:** of those regions, the ones
  without a genome-wide significant SNP (largest SNP |z| < 5.45).

```{r top5_pip_z_setup}
pzt <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_top5_pip_z.tsv")); z1 <- pzt[run == "est"]; z3 <- pzt[run == "esh"]; z5 <- pzt[run == "esf"]
```

![](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/isoqtl_top5_pip_z.png)

[Open as PDF](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/isoqtl_top5_pip_z.pdf)

Each point is one molecular trait (an eQTL gene, an sQTL intron or an isoform) in
a fine-mapped region of the joint run (`r fmt(z1$traits)` traits with the top SNP,
`r fmt(z3$traits)` with the top 3, `r fmt(z5$traits)` with the top 5): its `susie_pip` against its own
GWAS |z|. The dashed lines mark `susie_pip` 0.8 and |z| 3, and the shaded corner holds the
suspect traits. With the top SNP, `r z1$traits_pip08_z_lt3` of the `r z1$traits_pip08`
traits at `susie_pip` &ge; 0.8 have |z| < 3; with the top 3, `r z3$traits_pip08_z_lt3` of
`r z3$traits_pip08` (`r z3$isoqtl_pip08_z_lt3` isoQTL traits); with the top 5, `r z5$traits_pip08_z_lt3`
of `r z5$traits_pip08` (`r z5$isoqtl_pip08_z_lt3` isoQTL traits). With multiple SNPs, many isoQTL
traits also sit at `susie_pip` 1 with only moderate |z|.

**Example region** `r sn$region_id` in the eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 5) run.
SuSiE puts `r sprintf("%.2f", rg$region_trait_pip[1])` of its 5 effects on isoQTL
traits and `r sprintf("%.2f", rg$region_snp_pip[1])` on SNPs, although the strongest
SNP (`r sn$molecular_id`) has z = `r sprintf("%.2f", sn$z)`.

```{r top5_region}
knitr::kable(rg[, .(Type=type, gene_name=fifelse(is.na(gene_name), "&ndash;", gene_name), `Trait or SNP`=sub(".*__", "", molecular_id),
  z=sprintf("%.2f", z), susie_pip=sprintf("%.2f", susie_pip), SNPs=n_snps)], escape=FALSE, align="lllrrr")
```

Traits with `susie_pip` &ge; 0.2 in the region, and its strongest SNP. **SNPs:**
the SNPs in the trait's weights. `r unique(rt[duplicated(gene_name), gene_name])`'s two isoforms
are copies of one trait (`susie_pip` 0.50 each).

`r ex5$gene_name[1]`'s isoform `r sub(".*__", "", ex5$molecular_id[1])` gets `susie_pip`
`r sprintf("%.2f", ex5$trait_susie_pip[1])` with z = `r sprintf("%.2f", ex5$trait_z[1])`. Its SNPs:

```{r top5_example}
rc <- grep("^r_", names(ex5), value=TRUE)
x <- ex5[, c(list(SNP=snp, Region=snp_region, weight=sprintf("%.3f", weight), `GWAS z`=sprintf("%.2f", gwas_z)),
             lapply(.SD, function(v) sprintf("%.2f", v))), .SDcols=rc]
setnames(x, rc, paste("r with", sub("^r_", "", rc)))
knitr::kable(x, align=c("l", "l", rep("r", ncol(x) - 2)))
```

- **weight:** the weight cTWAS used (the model weight scaled by
  `scale_predictdb_weights`).
- **r with ...:** LD between the trait's SNPs (UKB reference), as cTWAS uses it.
  cTWAS sets it to 0 between SNPs in different regions.

The two largest weights, `r sprintf("%.2f", e2$weight[1])` on `r e2$snp[1]` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", e2$weight[2])` on `r e2$snp[2]`, have opposite signs on SNPs in LD
(r = `r sprintf("%.2f", r12)`), so much of the trait is the difference between
these two SNPs. Its z-score, which sums all 5 SNPs' weighted z-scores, is near 0.
Such pairs are more common among the suspect traits. In the joint run,
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * gcl("susie_pip >= 0.8, |z| < 3")$share_opposite_pair_r08)` of the
`r gcl("susie_pip >= 0.8, |z| < 3")$traits` isoQTL traits with `susie_pip` &ge; 0.8 and |z| < 3 have
two SNPs with weights of opposite sign and |r| &ge; 0.8. The share is
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * gcl("susie_pip >= 0.8, |z| >= 3")$share_opposite_pair_r08)` for those
with |z| &ge; 3 and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * gcl("susie_pip < 0.8")$share_opposite_pair_r08)` for
the other fine-mapped isoQTL traits.

**Our reading, not tested:** keeping 5 SNPs of a dense model can keep such
opposite-sign pairs. A trait like this can fit differences between the GWAS
z-scores of SNPs in LD, for example where the UKB LD reference does not match
the GWAS samples (LD mismatch). That would inflate both the isoQTL prior and
the gene PIPs. **Post-processing changes this picture** ([below](#post-processing)):
after region merging almost none of these traits keeps its PIP, and the
LD-mismatch check refits the traits of only 2 genes, so the main cause looks like
region boundaries rather than LD mismatch.

### By run {.tabset}

Genes with `combined_pip` of at least 0.5.

```{r gene_tabs, results="asis"}
for (r in names(RUNS)) {
  cat("#### ", RUNS[[r]], "\n\n", sep="")
  cat(gene_table(r, g[run == r & combined_pip >= 0.5]), "\n\n", sep="")
}
```

- **eQTL_pip** and the other PIP columns appear when a run has more than one QTL type.
- **Traits:** the gene's molecular traits in fine-mapped regions, over all QTL types.
- **Top trait:** the trait with the largest `susie_pip`: its ID (an eQTL gene, an
  sQTL intron or an isoform), type, `susie_pip` and z-score (z).
- **isoQTL copies** (isoQTL runs only): see [Duplicate isoQTL traits](#duplicate-isoqtl-traits).

## Post-processing

```{r pp_setup}
pps <- fread(file.path(A, "pp_summary.tsv")); ppz <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_pp_pip_z.tsv"))
ppg <- fread(file.path(A, "pp_gene_pips.tsv")); ppx <- fread(file.path(A, "isoqtl_pp_example.tsv"))
PPR <- c(est="eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 1)", esh="eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 3)", esf="eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 5)")
zc <- function(q, st, col) ppz[run == q & stage == st][[col]]
e1 <- ppg[run == "est" & (combined_pip_before >= 0.8 | combined_pip_after >= 0.8)]
amt <- function(q, st) sprintf("%.2f", ppx[run == q & stage == st, susie_pip])
```

**How it was done** (ours, following the M-cTWAS paper's pipeline and its settings;
ctwas 0.6.1), for the three eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL runs:

1. **Region merging** (`postprocess_region_merging()`). cTWAS fine-maps each LD
   region on its own, with no LD between SNPs of different regions. A gene whose
   traits use SNPs in more than one region is split across them. For every such
   boundary gene with PIP &ge; 0.5 (`pip_thresh = 0.5`, `filter_cs = FALSE`), the
   regions are merged and fine-mapped again with their full LD, using the run's
   `group_prior` and `group_prior_var`, L = 5 and up to 20,000 SNPs.
2. **LD mismatch** (`postprocess_LD_mismatch()`). In regions whose molecular traits'
   credible-set PIPs sum to more than 0.2, each SNP's z-score is compared with the
   value its neighbours predict under the UKB LD reference; SNPs that disagree
   (p < 5e-6) are flagged. A trait with PIP &ge; 0.2 whose prediction model uses a
   flagged SNP is problematic, and its region is fine-mapped again without LD
   (identity correlation, L = 1, the same z-scores and priors). This is a
   robustness check, not a repair: losing PIP there does not by itself prove an
   artefact.
3. **Gene PIPs** recomputed as before (`combine_gene_pips()`, `by = "type"`,
   `method = "combine_cs"`, `filter_cs = FALSE`).

**Not redone:** the parameter estimation. `group_prior`, `log_enrichment` and
`prop_heritability` in the tables above are from the original fits. Each run's
weights and GWAS z-scores were checked against its input record.

```{r pp_table}
knitr::kable(pps[match(names(PPR), run), .(Run=PPR[run], `Boundary genes (rows)`=sprintf("%d (%d)", boundary_genes, boundary_rows),
  `Merged regions`=merged_regions, `Regions checked for LD mismatch`=ld_regions_checked, `Flagged SNPs`=fmt(problematic_snps),
  `Traits refit without LD (genes)`=sprintf("%d (%d)", problematic_traits, problematic_trait_genes),
  `Genes, combined_pip >= 0.8: before / after`=sprintf("%d / %d", genes_pip08_before, genes_pip08_after),
  `Traits, susie_pip >= 0.8 and |z| < 3: before / after`=vapply(run, function(q) sprintf("%d / %d", zc(q, "before", "traits_pip08_z_lt3"), zc(q, "after", "traits_pip08_z_lt3")), ""))],
  align="lrrrrrrr")
```

- **Boundary genes (rows):** distinct genes selected for merging; a gene can give
  several rows. **Merged regions:** the new regions after merging.
- **Flagged SNPs:** SNPs whose z-score disagrees with the LD reference. **Traits refit
  without LD:** traits that use a flagged SNP and have PIP &ge; 0.2, with their genes
  in brackets (top 5: `r pps[run == "esf", problematic_gene_names]`).
- **Traits with |z| < 3:** the suspect corner of the figure below.

![](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/isoqtl_pp_pip_z.png)

[Open as PDF](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/isoqtl_pp_pip_z.pdf)

The same figure as in [the checks](#top-3-and-top-5-snps-per-isoform-checks), after
post-processing: each molecular trait's `susie_pip` against its own GWAS |z|.

**What changed:**

- **Top 1:** nothing material. The same `r pps[run == "est", genes_pip08_after]` genes are at
  `combined_pip` &ge; 0.8, and none moves by more than
  `r sprintf("%.2f", max(abs(e1$combined_pip_after - e1$combined_pip_before)))`.
- **Top 3 and top 5:** most of the excess genes go (`r pps[run == "esh", genes_pip08_before]` to
  `r pps[run == "esh", genes_pip08_after]` and `r pps[run == "esf", genes_pip08_before]` to
  `r pps[run == "esf", genes_pip08_after]`), and so do nearly all the high-PIP traits
  with |z| < 3. AMT's isoform, the example above, goes from `susie_pip`
  `r amt("esh", "before")` to `r amt("esh", "after")` (top 3) and from `r amt("esf", "before")` to
  `r amt("esf", "after")` (top 5).
- **Our reading:** the excess came mainly from region boundaries, not LD mismatch.
  The LD-mismatch step refit the traits of only 2 genes. Many top-3 and top-5
  isoQTL traits use SNPs in two neighbouring regions (one of AMT's 5 SNPs is in
  the next region); fine-mapped region by region, with no LD between regions, such
  traits took PIP that they lose once the regions are merged.
- **Caveat:** the parameters were not re-estimated, so the top-3 and top-5
  enrichment and `prop_heritability` above still come from the original fits and
  are likely inflated.

### Genes after post-processing {.tabset}

Genes with `combined_pip` &ge; 0.8 after post-processing.

```{r pp_genes, results="asis"}
for (q in names(PPR)) {
  cat("#### ", PPR[[q]], "\n\n", sep="")
  d <- ppg[run == q & combined_pip_after >= 0.8][order(-combined_pip_after)]
  x <- d[, .(gene_name, `combined_pip before`=cell(combined_pip_before), `combined_pip after`=cell(combined_pip_after),
             `eQTL_pip after`=cell(eQTL_pip_after), `sQTL_pip after`=cell(sQTL_pip_after), `isoQTL_pip after`=cell(isoQTL_pip_after))]
  cat(paste(knitr::kable(x, escape=FALSE, align="lrrrrr"), collapse="\n"), "\n\n", sep="")
}
```

"&ndash;": the gene has no trait of that type in a fine-mapped region. The before
and after values for every gene and QTL type are in
[pp_gene_pips.tsv](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/pp_gene_pips.tsv).

### Top 1, top 3 and top 5 compared, after post-processing

```{r pp_venn_setup}
gcat <- fread(file.path(A, "pp_gene_categories.tsv"), na.strings=c("", "NA"))
nc <- function(k) gcat[category == k, .N]; npr <- function(k) gcat[category == k & promising == TRUE, .N]
cat_table <- function(k) {
  d <- gcat[category == k & promising == TRUE]
  d[, sl := fifelse(is.na(shared_locus), "", shared_locus)]   # empty: no other gene of the diagram at this locus
  d <- d[order(-(!nzchar(sl) & !mhc), -region_max_snp_absz)]
  note <- fifelse(d$mhc, "MHC", fifelse(nzchar(d$sl), paste("same locus as", d$sl), ""))
  x <- d[, .(gene_name, `PIP top 1`=cell(pip_top1), `PIP top 3`=cell(pip_top3), `PIP top 5`=cell(pip_top5), Driver=driver,
             `Trait z`=sprintf("%.1f", top_z), `Region |z|`=sprintf("%.1f", region_max_snp_absz),
             `Catalog SCZ hits (best p)`=fifelse(catalog_n > 0, sprintf("%d (%s)", catalog_n, fp(catalog_best_p)), "0"), Note=note)]
  paste(knitr::kable(x, escape=FALSE, align="lrrrlrrrl"), collapse="\n")
}
notp <- function(k) { x <- gcat[category == k & promising == FALSE, gene_name]; if (length(x)) paste(x, collapse=", ") else "none" }
```

![](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/pp_gene_venn.png)

[Open as PDF](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/pp_gene_venn.pdf)

Genes with `combined_pip` &ge; 0.8 after post-processing in the three runs. Circle
areas are proportional to the number of genes (an `eulerr` fit; three circles
cannot match every overlap exactly, so each region shows its true count).

**Promising** (our rule, from our data only): the gene sits at a genome-wide
significant locus, meaning the strongest SNP in its top trait's region has
|z| > 5.45 (p < 5e-8) or the GWAS Catalog (2026-10-22) has a schizophrenia
association with p &le; 5e-8 within 500 kb, **and** its own top trait has
|z| &ge; 3. Genes in the MHC, or at a locus where another gene of the diagram is
also found, are kept but noted. SCZ loci are dense, so the rule supports the locus
more than the gene, and the literature has not been checked.

```{r pp_venn_lists, results="asis"}
heads <- c(`1. top 3 and top 5`="Found by both top 3 and top 5", `2. top 3 only`="Top 3 only", `3. top 5 only`="Top 5 only", `4. top 1 only`="Top 1 only")
for (k in names(heads)) {
  cat("#### ", heads[[k]], " (", npr(k), " of ", nc(k), " promising)\n\n", sep="")
  cat(cat_table(k), "\n\nNot promising: ", notp(k), ".\n\n", sep="")
}
```

- **PIP top 1 / 3 / 5:** `combined_pip` after post-processing in each run; "&ndash;": not in
  a fine-mapped region of that run. **Driver:** the QTL type with the largest PIP.
- **Trait z:** the GWAS z-score of the gene's top trait (largest `susie_pip`), in the
  run where the gene's `combined_pip` is largest. **Region |z|:** the strongest SNP in
  that trait's region after merging.
- **Catalog SCZ hits:** GWAS Catalog associations with schizophrenia (p &le; 5e-8)
  within 500 kb of the gene, and the best p.

**Short reading (ours):** the most convincing new genes are those both multi-SNP
runs agree on, at strong loci: FOXM1, POLR3H, AP3B2, PPIP5K1 and HRCT1; CUX2 is
the strongest gene found by top 3 only. Genes found by only one of top 3 and top 5
are less robust, since 3 rather than 5 SNPs per isoform should not change the
causal gene; the MHC genes and the chr3p21 cluster switch between the runs. Most
top-1-only genes stay just below 0.8 in the multi-SNP runs, where isoQTL traits
compete for the same signal. The top-3 and top-5 priors were not re-estimated
after merging, so their PIPs may still be a little optimistic. All genes:
[pp_gene_categories.tsv](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/pp_gene_categories.tsv).

## All genes

```{r all_genes}
DT::datatable(as.data.frame(g[, .(Run=RUNS[run], gene_name, combined_pip=round(combined_pip, 3), eQTL_pip=round(eQTL_pip, 3), sQTL_pip=round(sQTL_pip, 3),
  irQTL_pip=round(irQTL_pip, 3), isoQTL_pip=round(isoQTL_pip, 3), Traits=n_traits, `Top trait`=top_trait, `Top trait type`=top_type, `susie_pip (top trait)`=round(top_trait_pip, 3),
  z=round(z, 2), `isoQTL copies`=top_isoqtl_copies)][order(-combined_pip)]), rownames=FALSE, filter="top", extensions="Buttons",
  options=list(pageLength=10, scrollX=TRUE, dom="Bfrtip", buttons=c("copy", "csv")), caption="Every gene in a fine-mapped region, in every run.")
```

**Code:** `long_read_RNA/15.ctwas_gtex_isoform/`:

- `0.build_isoform_topqtl.R`: the irQTL top-QTL weights and their mapping table.
- `3.fetch_isotwas_models.sh`: fetches the Brain Cerebellum isoTWAS models from
  Zenodo (only the byte range that holds them, on the login node).
- `4.build_isoqtl_isotwas.R`: the isoQTL weights (top 1, or top K SNPs with a
  second argument) and their mapping table.
- `1.run_ctwas.R` and `.sbatch`: the nine runs (QTL types `es`, `esi`, `i`, `est`,
  `t`, `esh`, `h`, `esf` and `f`; `h` and `f` are the top-3 and top-5 isoQTL weights).
- `2.summarize.R`: this page's tables and figures.
- `5.top5_diagnostics.R`: the checks of the top-3 and top-5 runs.
- `6.postprocess.R` and `.sbatch`: post-processing (region merging, LD mismatch, gene PIPs) of one run.
- `7.pp_pip_z.R`, `8.pp_summarize.R` and `9.pp_gene_venn.R`: this page's post-processing figures and tables.
